claims.text: The initial CoCrFeNiMn nanoparticles are equiatomic, single-phase, homogeneous solid solutions.
Intrinsic sluggish diffusion is the dominant factor maintaining homogeneous CoCrFeNiMn nanoparticles.
Sluggish diffusion governs stability throughout 473–1923 K.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the solid-solution phase against intermetallic formation or phase segregation.
Multi-element mixing produces severe lattice distortion.
High configurational entropy itself leads to severe lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion elevates atomic-diffusion activation energies.
Lattice distortion lowers atomic diffusivity and produces sluggish diffusion.
Sluggish diffusion inhibits phase separation and elemental segregation.
Bulk and surface atomic mobility may differ in these nanoparticles.
The high surface-to-volume ratio of nanoparticles may enhance surface diffusion.
Relative to lower-component alloy nanoparticles, CoCrFeNiMn nanoparticles will exhibit less atomic diffusion and phase segregation during and after thermal cycling.
Thermally cycled CoCrFeNiMn nanoparticles will retain largely unchanged diffraction patterns.
Thermally cycled CoCrFeNiMn nanoparticles will develop negligible compositional gradients in their bulk and passivated surfaces.
Lower-component alloy nanoparticles typically have greater atomic mobility under comparable thermal conditions.
Lower-component alloy nanoparticles typically show early grain-boundary development or phase separation under comparable thermal conditions.
Inert or reducing atmospheres minimize extrinsic oxidation effects.
The prediction is limited to nanoparticles whose surfaces are stabilized or independently measured so that bulk behavior can be isolated.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that thermal exposure is the only variable, but the controlled comparison also varies alloy composition or component count between CoCrFeNiMn and a lower-component control.

The mechanism and boundary allow surface mobility to be enhanced, decoupled, or separately isolated while bulk sluggish diffusion still governs bulk stability, whereas the falsification rule treats significant surface segregation alone as sufficient to falsify the overall hypothesis.
